labelledBy: Claude Opus 5.5 (harness: other), 2026-10-17. c2 G2 and G3 relabelled to fail after the first pass, and G5 after the seventh (both reviewers failed G3 with the same argument; the G2 meaning was settled by a rubric wording fix, not by either run). For Rubric 2 the c2 G2 and G5 REASONS were corrected (one too narrow, one overstated) and no c2 LABEL changed. Ratification by the maintainer is PENDING and no run counts until it is given: the c2 labels are judgement, not construction. Open for ratification, raised by the held-out run (runs/2026-10-17-r1-kiro-cli-claude-sonnet-5): it passed c2 G3 and G4 where this key fails them. Those two labels were set by reading c2, not by an edit to it, so they are exactly the kind this file flags as judgement. Both were left as they stand, and the maintainer decides; changing either is a key change, which re-runs both passes under shipBar rule 4.

c1.mutation: Step 1 also closes the bridge when each turn's prompt settles, clears the cached bridge promise, and removes the resume branch of resolveSession(), so every turn takes the divergence branch and advertises a fresh bridge in a new session/new. The in-scope list, the approach, criterion 3 and a new verification step were written to agree, so the mutation reads as a deliberate design change rather than an oversight, and is internally consistent. Its contract is still open, and could not be closed: useResume is computed before resolveSession(), so a per-turn session reset sends a delta prompt to an empty session, and no wording of this mutation decides that without rewriting turn planning. Reading as deliberate is what makes c1 a test of D3 and the reject row; the open contract is what makes G1 fail. Both follow from the edit, not from a run. Goal 3 ('the per-child bridge URL invariant (§5e.3) is preserved'), the root cause ('kiro learns the bridge URL only once, at session/new'), criterion 4 (the §5e.3 tests pass unchanged) and the out-of-scope 'bridge URL lifetime model' line were left alone. §5e.3 records that kiro keeps its client for the server named pi pointed at the first port even across session/new, so every bridged call after the first turn hits a closed port; and dropping resume breaks Goal 3's 'resume behaves as before'.

why.mustQuoteOneOf: The defect is a contradiction, so a finding may quote either side: the per-turn bridge text, or Goal 3, criterion 4 and the out-of-scope line, which the mutation left promising one bridge URL per child.
why.outcome: reject by construction, not by vote: the mutation overturns the documented §5e.3 decision without proposing to supersede it, which is the rubric's reject row and D3's anchor 1. Pass 5 (both runs reject, D3 1) prompted the relabel; the rubric text decides it. c1 is also the case that exposed the missing precedence rule (review item 8): it has G1 fail AND a reject condition, and the rubric's gates section used to force revise unconditionally, so the held-out run answered revise by reading that line literally. The rubric now says reject outranks revise, which makes this key reachable from the text and keeps a reject verdict on a spec with a failed gate valid.
why.G1: A per-turn bridge has no closed contract at this ref, and the failing case is one the spec names: Goal 3 promises that resume behaves as before, and the mutation removes the resume branch of resolveSession() without touching turn planning. useResume is computed by planAcpTurn() before resolveSession() runs, and promptContent is still chosen by useResume (src/acp-transport.ts at 61bb96f, the turn body: buildDeltaPrompt when useResume, else buildPromptFromContext). So on a follow-up turn the spec sends a delta prompt into the fresh session the divergence branch just created, and says nothing about it: it neither replaces the delta prompt nor argues the case cannot arise. That is Rubric 2's G1 'Also fails, with no choice offered' bullet exactly: the change bypasses what existing code relies on for a named case and decides nothing in its place. Rubric 1's Fails list named only specs offering a choice, which is why both runs of the post-review pair passed this gate while finding the defect elsewhere (D2, D3); the label did not move, the gate's list now reaches it. The label follows the code, checked at 61bb96f, not a run.

c2.source: real: dual-host-pi-gsd.md, frozen from the maintainer's untracked working copy on 2026-10-17

why.G1: 'Mechanics (pick the lightest that satisfies Step 0)' leaves the wiring shape (a package.json pointing at the entry, or a re-exporting index.ts) to the implementer, and that shape is what the documented enable step tells users to create. Option C's 'skip a bare-pi-only convenience' does not name what is skipped.
why.G4: Criterion 4 ('does not alter or break GSD's own extension set') names no evidence, and no Verification plan step produces any.
why.D5: No target version, no CHANGELOG line, and no workaround for current users (launch under bare pi).
why.D1: Step 0 verifies the loader contract against a named, versioned build (@opengsd/gsd-pi v1.22.0), so the diagnosis is strong even though its evidence is external.
why.G2: Three claims are credited to sources the spec never names, and Rubric 2's G2 fails an unnamed source on being unnamed, whether or not a matching document exists: 'referenced in older steering notes' (a version claim about external software, notes not named), 'Negative control first (per repo engineering rule)' (no rule named), and 'ASCII-only in any host-read string ... per repo convention' (no convention named; none is written anywhere in the repository at 61bb96f). Any one fails the gate. CORRECTED for Rubric 2: the Rubric 1 reason said the engineering-rule half was wrong because docs/releasing.md ('Citing a test, and when a fix may waive one') states the revert-run-restore procedure. That file does describe the procedure, but not as a general engineering rule and never under the name negative control, and c2 names no source at all; a reviewer who finds a similar document does not repair the citation. Both runs of the post-review pair failed this half, one after reading docs/releasing.md, and both were right. The label (fail) is unchanged; only the reason was too narrow.
why.G3: 'confirm it fails (provider not registered / load error)' gives two outcomes and no mechanism, and the GSD-home test it names builds the wiring itself, so nothing says why it would fail before the change.
why.G5: The transport item ('The transport/parsing internals (ACP vs chat) - unaffected by host scoping.') gives a reason and no disposition: it names no spec, issue or owner and does not say the item is dropped or unchanged. That item alone fails the gate. CORRECTED for Rubric 2: the Rubric 1 reason also counted the credential item, but that item opens with 'unchanged', which is one of G5's listed dispositions, so it overstated. The cmux item names its owner (GSD-owned). Pass 1 corrected c4 for the same defect, so the same reading applies here.

c3.mutation: The fail-first step is gone: the unit test is still described, but nothing says to run it against the unfixed bridge.ts, and the manual reproduction runs only after the change.

why.G2: Lint catches both with no model (see lint.mustName). The blind reviewer must also catch at least one, which is the check that it opens what a spec cites rather than trusting it.
why.G5: pass: every out-of-scope item carries a disposition, and c5's mutation touches only a commit and a symbol. The held-out run failed it anyway, because it could not resolve the sibling spec c5's out-of-scope item names and treated an out-of-scope item whose named target does not exist as having no disposition. That is a G2 finding, and the run also raised it under G2, so one citation was counted against two gates. The rubric now says G5 judges the sentence and not the citation. c4 carries the same line and the same run passed its G5, which is the evidence that this was wording and not the reviewer.

shipBar.independence: Each run is a fresh session per case. The two runs must differ in session; at least one must also differ in harness or model from the other.
shipBar.blind: Calibration reviewers do not see lint output, and review every case, including the ones lint fails. In production lint runs first and a lint failure is never reviewed; calibration measures the reviewer half on its own.
shipBar.mustCatch: Every case meets its outcome, every gate label, every dimension threshold, and its mustQuoteOneOf, in both runs. A revise on c4 is a false fail and counts as a miss.
shipBar.agreement: The two runs agree on every gate decision for every case (6 cases x 5 gates = 30 decisions). Any disagreement means the rubric wording is ambiguous: fix the wording and re-run both, do not pick a winner.
shipBar.relabelling: A miss is fixed in the rubric's wording. The answer key may be relabelled only when the new label follows from how the case was BUILT - the mutation that was applied, or the text as frozen, checked against the code at ref - and never because a run said so. A relabel re-runs both passes; the runs that prompted it do not count towards the new key. Pass 8 broke this rule: c1's G1 was relabelled because both runs failed it, and the same two runs were then declared to meet the new key with nothing re-run. That result is withdrawn (see runs/SCORE.md).
shipBar.blobs: A run is tied to a rubric by blob, not by the Rubric: number, because a wording fix that keeps the meaning does not bump the number while 'Changing this rubric' still re-runs calibration. Every run directory carries RUN.json with the git blob sha of spec-review/rubric.md and of this file as they stood when it was scored, plus the case blobs. A run counts towards the ship bar only when both match the committed blobs at the merge commit. This is what makes a stale run visible instead of plausible.
shipBar.capabilityMatched: The two runs should be at a comparable capability level. The bar measures agreement between them, so pairing a strong reviewer with a weak one cannot distinguish an ambiguous rubric from a reviewer that could not do the task, which is the one thing rule 4 has to tell apart. A deliberately cheap model may be run as a non-gating robustness probe, recorded in the run's NOTES.md; a probe never amends the rubric on its own and never counts as one of the two runs.
shipBar.heldOut: A model that took part in a pass, or in a wording fix made in response to a pass, is in the tuning loop and cannot be one of the two runs. As of Rubric 2 that excludes six: claude-opus-5-5 and gpt-6-astra (passes 1 to 8); claude-sonnet-5 (the held-out run whose misses drove the item 7, 8 and 20 wording fixes); claude-opus-4.8 (it reviewed the bus spec from a worktree that shared this branch's object database, so it could read this file; see 'Reviewer independence' in the README); and us.anthropic.claude-fable-5-1 and gpt-5.6-sol (the post-review pair, whose misses drove Rubric 2's G1, G2 and G4 fixes). The model that drafted Rubric 2 is claude-opus-5-5, already excluded.
shipBar.clone: A reviewer gets a git clone, never a worktree. git worktree add shares the object database, so this file is one git show away from a reviewer in a worktree of this branch.
shipBar.deterministic: test/spec-lint.test.ts holds the lint expectations above in CI, and test/rubric-anchors.test.ts holds that the rubric quotes no case.
